fatal_errors: The proposed mechanical-alloying intervention does not reconstruct the controlled annealing, elastic strain, or ribbon-spacing interventions.

The claimed beneficial role of increased lattice distortion conflicts with the target mechanism, in which annealing-induced strain relaxation and short-range atomic reordering reduce pinning and enhance ferromagnetic alignment.
The proposed 250–350 K and below-2 T regime does not match the demonstrated broad response around 40–200 K, whose reported peak was measured at 140 K and 5 T.
The predicted entropy change above 2 J kg−1 K−1 is inconsistent with the observed increase from approximately 1.25 to 1.35 J kg−1 K−1.
Rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability are asserted without supporting evidence or adequate measurements.
Mechanical alloying simultaneously changes grain size, defect density, phase constitution, contamination, and magnetic disorder, so the proposed experiment cannot isolate lattice distortion.
explanation: The response addresses the general magnetocaloric design problem and gives a nominally falsifiable trend, but it neither reconstructs the studied Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 thin-film/nanoribbon system nor its decisive interventions. Its mechanism is largely opposite to the supported result: structural relaxation and reduced internal strain improved exchange and reduced pinning without crystallization, while elastic strain had a separate magnetoelastic effect above 100 K. The numerical performance thresholds, operating range, and boundaries are arbitrary and unsupported. No prior evidence is cited, and the experiment omits direct hysteresis and mechanical-integrity tests while using a highly confounded intervention.
